title: 62M with crushing chest pain
presentation: A 62-year-old man presents to the emergency department with 90 minutes of crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm, associated with diaphoresis and nausea. Blood pressure 148/92 mmHg, heart rate 104 bpm, oxygen saturation 96% on room air. ECG shows ST elevation of 4 mm in leads V2-V4 with reciprocal ST depression in inferior leads. High-sensitivity troponin is 2.4 ng/mL (reference <0.04 ng/mL). He has hypertension and hyperlipidemia and smokes one pack per day.

title: 34F with thunderclap headache
presentation: A 34-year-old woman presents with sudden onset of the worst headache of her life, described as a thunderclap headache, with photophobia and neck stiffness. On examination she is drowsy but arousable, with nuchal rigidity. Non-contrast head CT shows hyperdense blood in the basal cisterns and Sylvian fissures. Blood pressure 172/104 mmHg, heart rate 92 bpm. No focal neurologic deficits on brief examination.

title: 71M with acute dyspnea after flight
presentation: A 71-year-old man presents with acute onset dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain 6 hours after a 9-hour international flight. Heart rate 118 bpm, blood pressure 108/70 mmHg, oxygen saturation 89% on room air, respiratory rate 26/min. Right calf is swollen and tender. D-dimer is 2400 ng/mL (reference <500 ng/mL). CT pulmonary angiography shows a filling defect in the right main pulmonary artery.

title: 45F with polyuria and weight loss
presentation: A 45-year-old woman presents with 3 weeks of polyuria, polydipsia, and unintentional weight loss of 8 kg, now with nausea and abdominal pain. She is tachypneic with deep Kussmaul respirations and fruity breath odor. Fingerstick glucose is 420 mg/dL. Arterial blood gas shows pH 7.28, bicarbonate 14 mmol/L. Urinalysis is strongly positive for ketones. Serum potassium is 5.1 mmol/L.

title: 28M with fever after hotel stay
presentation: A 28-year-old man presents with 5 days of high fever to 103.2 F, dry cough, headache, and watery diarrhea. He returned 10 days ago from a conference where he stayed in a hotel with a decorative fountain in the lobby. Sodium is 128 mmol/L. Chest X-ray shows a right lower lobe infiltrate. He is a non-smoker with no chronic illnesses. Urinary antigen testing is pending.

title: 55M with epigastric pain radiating to back
presentation: A 55-year-old man presents with 12 hours of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, with nausea and two episodes of vomiting. He drinks approximately 6 beers daily. On examination he has epigastric tenderness without guarding. Serum lipase is 1200 U/L (reference 13-60 U/L). Abdominal CT shows peripancreatic fat stranding without necrosis. Triglycerides are 180 mg/dL and calcium is 9.2 mg/dL.

title: 60F with edema and heavy proteinuria
presentation: A 60-year-old woman presents with 2 months of progressive bilateral leg edema and periorbital puffiness. 24-hour urine protein is 6.2 g/day. Serum albumin is 2.4 g/dL, total cholesterol 340 mg/dL. Serum creatinine is 1.1 mg/dL. Urinalysis shows oval fat bodies and no red blood cell casts. Blood pressure is 138/84 mmHg. Renal ultrasound shows normal-sized kidneys.

title: 8F with target lesions after antibiotics
presentation: An 8-year-old girl presents with 3 days of painful targetoid skin lesions on the trunk and extremities with erosions of the oral mucosa and lip crusting. Lesions began 10 days after starting trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole for a urinary tract infection. She is febrile to 101.8 F. Nikolsky sign is negative. Estimated body surface area involvement is under 10%.
